lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- What Is Happening Right Now
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Marcos Aurélio Miranda de Moura | Lesson 4 -- What Is Happening Right Now
lesson.grammar_point: present continuous and its contrast with the present simple

paras: Good morning. Three things are moving this week and one of them is not moving fast enough, so I am starting with that one. We are running about a week behind on the price list rollout. The bottleneck is the label supplier, not the plant, and we are splitting the order between two suppliers from Thursday. I am not asking anybody to fix it. I am asking for a decision on the split.

The workshop pilot is going well. It is currently running in twelve workshops in one state, and the early numbers are better than we expected. I am not calling it a success yet. We are waiting four more weeks, because the first month of any pilot flatters itself.

The conversation with the new distributor is ongoing and nothing is signed. They are asking for a discount we are not going to give, so we are talking about volume instead. That one is temporary in a good way: it either closes in September or it does not, and either answer is useful.
reading.source: Simulated internal e-mail, written for this lesson -- not a published document

choices: To report three results the team achieved last month
To say where three things stand today and ask for one decision
To announce a new distributor contract

items: The writer starts with the project that is late.
He says three things are moving and one is not moving fast enough, so he starts with that one.
The pilot has already been declared a success.
He says he is not calling it a success yet, and that they are waiting four more weeks.
The bottleneck is inside the plant.
The text says the bottleneck is the label supplier, not the plant.
The e-mail asks the reader for a decision.
He asks for a decision on splitting the label order between two suppliers.

listenings.text: Ninety seconds, three things, and I am starting with the one that is late. The price list rollout is running about a week behind. The bottleneck is the label supplier, not the plant, and we are splitting the order between two suppliers from Thursday. Second, the pilot. It is currently running in twelve workshops and the early numbers look good, better than we expected, but I am not calling it a success. I am waiting four more weeks, because the first month of a pilot always flatters itself. Third, the new distributor. That conversation is ongoing and nothing is signed. They are asking for a discount and we are not giving it, so we are talking about volume instead. One decision from this room today, and it is the label order. Everything else can wait a week.

Most status updates say nothing, and they say it at considerable length. What they are actually doing is listing activity. We are reviewing this, we are aligning on that, we are working with the agency. All true, all useless, and all it proves is that people are busy, which nobody doubted. A good update answers two questions and stops. What is different since last week, and what decision is somebody waiting for. If the answer to the first one is nothing, say nothing and give the time back. And one word I would delete from every status meeting in the world. Fine. A project is fine, and fine, and fine, right up to the week it is not, and then everybody is surprised except the person who knew in March. Fine is the most expensive word in the room.
